text:
Alec: Heads up — big retry spike on svc/gpu-infer in us-west-2, ~10x RTOs since 02:10 UTC. Latency tails and lots of 502/504. Dash: https://dash.redwood/internal/d/abc123

infra-bot: ALERT: svc/gpu-infer (us-west-2) 12m error rate > 8% — auto-signal triggered by latency-slo-watchdog

Sophia: Which capacity pool? Dedicated or shared?

Alec: Dedicated-GPU-pool-a (A100s). ipvs shows extremely uneven endpoint distribution — most connections pinned to 2 nodes.

Ram: Can you paste ipvsadm -Ln and kubectl get endpoints svc/gpu-infer -o wide?

Alec: Sure, snippets below:
```
# ipvsadm -Ln
IP Virtual Server version 1.2.1 (size=4096)
Prot LocalAddress:Port Scheduler Flags
  -> RemoteAddress:Port           Forward Weight ActiveConn InActConn
TCP  10.3.12.5:443 rr
  -> 10.2.11.21:12000            Masq    1      1423       0
  -> 10.2.11.22:12000            Masq    1      18         0
  -> 10.2.11.23:12000            Masq    1      14         0
  -> 10.2.11.24:12000            Masq    1      8          0

# kubectl get endpoints gpu-infer -o wide
ENDPOINTS                       NODE
10.2.11.21:12000                g-a100-21
10.2.11.22:12000                g-a100-22
10.2.11.23:12000                g-a100-23
10.2.11.24:12000                g-a100-24
```

Alec: See the ActiveConn column — 10.2.11.21 is taking >90% of active conns.

Lina: Any recent infra changes? We rolled a kernel update and an HCA firmware push ~2h ago in that AZ.

Alec: dmesg shows rdma: device mlx5_0: port 1 down -> fallback to tcp. Also repeated "NETDEV WATCHDOG" on 10.2.11.21. tcpdump shows MSS clamping and retransmits.

Sophia: That smells like MTU/RDMA path asymmetry. What does ethtool show for MTU and offloads?

Alec: Ran ethtool on g-a100-21:
```
# ethtool -k eth0
Features for eth0:
rx-checksumming: on
large-receive-offload: off
GRO: off
SG: on

# ip link show dev eth0
3: eth0: mtu 1500 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
```
But other nodes show MTU 9000.

Ram: So MTU mismatch (1500 vs 9000) + RDMA fallback explains packet segmentation and heavy retransmit causing ipvs affinity to bias active connections to the node that still accepts full-sized frames. Also possible asymmetric routing at ToR.

infra-bot: NOTE: kernel-5.15.14-rc rolled to g-a100-21 02:05 UTC by deploy-bot

Sophia: Temporary mitigations:
- enable tcp_mtu_probing=1 to avoid PMTU blackhole
- mark node unschedulable for new affinity conn via ipvsadm --del-server? (but careful)

Ram: Also check kube-proxy mode/conntrack: if ipvs persistent conn is favoring an endpoint with stale path, conntrack will keep routing. Could reduce persistent timeout to force re-balance.

Alec: I'm cordoning g-a100-21 and draining non-critical pods now, starting graceful failover.

ops-bot: ACTION: cordon g-a100-21 requested by Alec at 02:26 UTC

Sophia: Good. We should also compare CNI MTU config (calico/flannel) — calico mtu 9000 expected. If the node reverted to 1500 during reboot, CNI didn't reconcile.

Lina: Also check HCA firmware: mlx5_core reported link event and fallback to ip_tcp in dmesg stack. If RNIC in wrong mode RoCE->IPoIB fallback happens.

Alec: Rolling restart kube-proxy on g-a100-21 to re-evaluate ipvs tables.

Sophia: Short-term knobs: tcp_mtu_probing=1, ipvs-persistent-scheduler tweak, kube-proxy restart. Longer-term: align MTU across infra, prevent kernel rollback on GPU nodes, upgrade RNIC firmware.

Irene: Creating an incident ticket and starting a postmortem draft. Early impact: ~30k extra requests retried, small but visible increase in GPU billing for the hour.

Alec: Commands I ran so far:
```
sudo cordon g-a100-21
sudo drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data g-a100-21 --grace-period=120
ssh g-a100-21 'sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1'
kubectl rollout restart daemonset/kube-proxy -n kube-system --field-selector spec.nodeName=g-a100-21
```

Ram: After drain, re-check ipvsadm -Ln and /proc/net/ip_vs_stats. If ActiveConn evens out, we can uncordon.

Sophia: Note for runbook: add MTU reconciliation check during node boot and a canary for RNIC firmware rollouts.

Lina: Cost/ops note: flagging Dedicated-GPU-pool-a for an audit of kernel/firmware sync. Someone from platform should own the audit.

Alec: I'll own the node drains and immediate monitoring. Will post when traffic evens and when we revert any temporary sysctl. :thumbsup:

Irene: Thanks — updating incident and tagging @oncall.

Alec: (02:55 UTC) update: after draining g-a100-21, ActiveConn distribution is now roughly even across endpoints, retry rate dropping back to baseline. Leaving cordon while we reconcile MTU and firmware.

Sophia: Great. Please add the exact kernel version and RNIC firmware to the postmortem.

Alec: Will do, closing thread when PM is up.
